source:
Zoë: The café’s late licence should be renewed. It’s the only place on Rue Ségur open after 23:00, and the owner has spent €4 000 on sound insulation — that’s more than the council asked for.
José: I don’t doubt the insulation. I’m saying residents on a residential street are entitled to quiet after eleven, full stop. “Only place open” is an argument for the customers, not for the people who live upstairs.
Zoë: The people upstairs signed the lease knowing there was a café below. A street isn’t a bedroom; a neighbourhood needs somewhere to be at midnight.
José: Knowing there was a café is not consenting to noise until two. Nobody’s entitlement to a night out outranks somebody’s entitlement to sleep.
Zoë: And nobody’s entitlement to sleep outranks a whole street’s right to have a life after dark. That’s the trade, and I’d make it the other way.
José: Then we agree on the facts and disagree on who the street is for.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should the café’s late licence on Rue Ségur be renewed?

positions.label: Renew the late licence
positions.thesis: The licence should be renewed because the café is the street’s only late venue and the owner has exceeded the council’s insulation requirements.
positions.steelman: Residents took their leases knowing a café was below, the owner has over-complied on sound, and a neighbourhood needs somewhere open after dark.

groundingQuotes.quote: The café’s late licence should be renewed.
a neighbourhood needs somewhere to be at midnight

positions.label: Do not renew
positions.thesis: The licence should not be renewed because residents of a residential street are entitled to quiet after eleven regardless of the insulation.
positions.steelman: Signing a lease above a café is not consent to noise until two, and no one’s night out outranks a resident’s sleep.

groundingQuotes.quote: residents on a residential street are entitled to quiet after eleven, full stop

claims.statement: A resident’s entitlement to sleep outranks anyone’s entitlement to a night out.

resolution.condition: The council states which entitlement governs on a residential street after eleven.

groundingQuotes.quote: Nobody’s entitlement to a night out outranks somebody’s entitlement to sleep.
I’d make it the other way

claims.statement: Taking a lease above a café amounts to accepting late-night activity below.

resolution.condition: Agree what a tenant consents to by signing a lease above a licensed venue.

groundingQuotes.quote: The people upstairs signed the lease knowing there was a café below.
Knowing there was a café is not consenting to noise until two.

commonGroundCandidates.statement: The owner has installed sound insulation beyond what the council asked for.

groundingQuotes.quote: the owner has spent €4 000 on sound insulation — that’s more than the council asked for

disagreementCandidates.question: Does a resident’s claim to quiet after eleven outrank the neighbourhood’s claim to a late venue?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Both accept the insulation facts; José ranks sleep above nightlife and Zoë ranks the street’s life after dark above an individual’s quiet.

participantStances.stance: Sleep outranks a night out on a residential street.
A street’s right to a life after dark outranks one tenant’s quiet.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Make the ranking explicit; no further evidence about the insulation changes it.

groundingQuotes.quote: Then we agree on the facts and disagree on who the street is for.

disagreementCandidates.question: Does taking a lease above a café count as consenting to late-night activity below?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Zoë treats the residents’ leases as acceptance of the café; José says knowing a café exists is not consent to noise until two.

participantStances.stance: They signed knowing the café was there.
Knowing is not consenting to noise until two.
